brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases placed linearly at q=-1,0,0, q=0,0,0 and q=1,0,0 (refs piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) forming a row of three joined cells.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: Bin hex-bin-full-drain installed in each cell (bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain) – full-depth drained trays with drainage holes.
Bins filled with soil and planted with young herbs (basil-young, mint-young, parsley-young) visible from above and oblique views; drained bins allow excess water to escape as required for herbs.

finish.summary: Built a linear 3-cell herb planter: three full hex bases side-by-side at -1,0,0 / 0,0,0 / 1,0,0, each fitted with a full-depth drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain). Caps and joint bolts applied per house rules, bins filled with soil and planted with basil, mint and parsley to demonstrate herb use. Mesh check clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
